div.div:
expalpo , āre, v. a., and expalpor , āri,
I.v. dep. a., to obtain by coaxing or flattery (ante-class.): “exora, blandire, expalpa,” Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 144 : si quid expalpare possim ab illo, Pompon. ap. Non. 104, 12: nunc servus argentum a patre expalpabitur, Plaut. Fragm, ap. Non. ib., and 476, 24.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
